script_and_orthography.writing_system: Scriptura continua (no word spaces, 1st-century BC Herculaneum Uncial bookhand)
script_and_orthography.sigma_form: Lunate sigma (C / Ϲ) exclusively; never standard four-stroke Σ
script_and_orthography.epsilon_form: Round / lunate epsilon (Є) with central crossbar
script_and_orthography.omega_form: Flat-bottomed or open double-loop uncial Ω
script_and_orthography.iota_adscript: Iota adscript written on the line (e.g., ΤΩΙ, ΤΗΙ, ΑΥΤΩΙ) rather than subscript
script_and_orthography.assimilation_at_sandhi: Frequent assimilation of final -ν before labials (ἐμ μέσῳ -> ΕΜΜΕCΩΙ) and gutturals (ἐγ γὰρ -> ΕΓΓΑΡ), documented by Crönert (1906)
script_and_orthography.hiatus_avoidance: Philodemus strictly avoids vowel hiatus across word boundaries via elision (δ', ἀλλ', κατ', ἐπ', οὐδ'), crasis (κἀν, τοὐναντίον), and selection of καθάπερ over καθώς

syllable_division_rules_at_line_end.rule_1_single_consonant: A single intervocalic consonant always goes with the FOLLOWING vowel on the next line (V-CV, e.g., Α-ΤΑ-ΡΑ-ΞΙ-Α, ΦΙ-ΛΟ-ΔΗ-ΜΟC).
syllable_division_rules_at_line_end.rule_2_double_or_liquid_nasal: Double consonants (ΛΛ, ΜΜ, ΝΝ, ΠΠ, CΚ/CC, ΤΤ) and liquid/nasal + stop clusters (ΜΠ, ΝΤ, ΓΚ, ΛΚ, ΡΓ, ΡΘ) split BETWEEN the two consonants (VC-CV, e.g., ΑΛ-ΛΑ, ΕΝ-ΤΑΥ-ΘΑ, ΟΡ-ΓΗ).
syllable_division_rules_at_line_end.rule_3_stop_plus_liquid: Stop + liquid/nasal clusters that can begin a Greek word (ΠΛ, ΠΡ, ΒΛ, ΒΡ, ΤΡ, ΚΛ, ΚΡ, ΦΛ, ΦΡ, ΧΡ, ΘΡ) stay together and move to the NEXT line (V-CCV, e.g., ΠΡΟ-ΛΗ-ΨΙC, Α-ΚΡΙ-ΒΩC).
syllable_division_rules_at_line_end.rule_4_compound_prepositions: Compound words divide after the prepositional prefix (e.g., ΠΡΟC-ΛΑΜ-ΒΑ-ΝΩ, CΥΝ-Ε-ΧΗC, ΕΚ-ΛΟ-ΓΗ).
syllable_division_rules_at_line_end.rule_5_forbidden_line_end_chars: A line in a Herculaneum column can NEVER end with a non-Greek-final single stop (Π, Β, Φ, Τ, Δ, Θ, Κ, Γ, Χ, Μ, Λ) unless it is the first half of a geminate/cluster split across lines.

marginal_marks_and_stichometry.paragraphos: A short horizontal ink stroke (—) placed beneath the first 2–3 letters of a line to signal a syntactic period or speaker/topic change WITHIN that line.
marginal_marks_and_stichometry.diple_obelos: Marginal forked mark (>—) or obelos indicating quotation or polemical citation of an opponent (e.g., Diogenes of Babylon, Carneades, Chrysippus).
marginal_marks_and_stichometry.koronis: Ornamental marginal flourish marking the major division or end of a treatise, immediately preceding the subscriptio colophon.
marginal_marks_and_stichometry.stichometry: Attic acrophonic or Ionian alphabetic numerals in the margin every 100 lines, plus total stichoi (ΑΡΙΘΜΟC XXX) and kollemata (ΚΟΛΛΗΜΑΤΑ XX) recorded beneath the author/title colophon.

ΠΡΟΛΗΨΙC.gloss: preconception / basic grasp of a concept

ΜΕΤΑΒΑCΙC.gloss: inductive transition from observed to unobserved

ΚΑΘΑΠΕΡ.gloss: just as (Philodemus's hiatus-avoiding form of καθώς/ὥσπερ)

ΜΕΛΛΟΝΤΑ.gloss: future things (attested in PHerc. Paris 4 at 1.1/2.4 um)
